newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED HELD 0-0 AT HOME BY VILLA, REMAIN THIRD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED HELD 0-0 AT HOME BY VILLA, REMAIN THIRD.

text.p: Manchester United were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw at home to Aston Villa on Wednesday and remain third in the English premier league, four points off the pace.

With leaders and arch-rivals Liverpool losing 1-0 at Chelsea earlier in the day, United had a chance to move back above Arsenal into second place and put the Merseysiders under more pressure at the top of the table.
But despite having the better of a hard-fought match at Old Trafford, the English champions, scorers of 10 goals in their last three league matches, could not find the net.
The match pitted the premier league's most prolific attack against its tightest defence. United have scored 42 league goals this season. Villa have conceded just 19.
United's Andy Cole, Ryan Giggs and Eric Cantona all missed clear-cut chances and in the end it was Villa's defence which won out.

Earlier, a solitary goal from Italian Roberto di Matteo was enough to seal Chelsea's victory over Liverpool and, with Arsenal and Newcastle both winning, the gap at the top of the table has been narrowed despite United's setback.

Chelsea, crushed 5-1 by Liverpool in the league at Anfield earlier this season, were forced to back-pedal for much of the first half as the visitors played their habitual patient passing game to near-perfection.

But di Matteo put Ruud Gullit's side ahead two minutes before halftime, capitalising on a mistake from Michael Thomas to run between the two centre-backs and score with a cool right-foot strike into the bottom left-hand corner of David James's net.

Chelsea kept their nerve after the interval and Mark Hughes almost put them 2-0 up when he crashed a shot against James's crossbar from a tight angle. In the end though, one goal was enough. Chelsea are seventh, level on points with sixth-placed Villa.

Arsenal beat Middlesbrough 2-0 to go back into second, two points behind Liverpool with a game in hand. Ian Wright scored Arsenal's second -- his 200th league goal -- after Dennis Bergkamp had sent the Gunners' on their way with a crisp volley from 25 metres after 15 minutes.

Fabrizio Ravanelli earned a chance to bring Middlesbrough back into the match when he was scythed down by Patrick Vieira in the penalty area, but the former Juventus striker thumped his spot-kick against the crossbar.
John Hartson was sent off for Arsenal, for whom disciplinary problems are becoming a serious threat to their trophy ambitions.
Wright, now just 12 goals short of the club's all-time scoring record, was playing his last game before starting a three-match suspension after being sent off at Nottingham Forest on December 21.

It was a disappointing day for Middlesbrough player-manager and former England captain Bryan Robson, who selected himself for the first time in over a year in response to Boro's crippling injury crisis.
Robson, an inspirational midfielder with Manchester United in the 1980s, turns 40 later this month. Wednesday's match was Robson's 568th league appearance.
While Robson was the oldest player on show in the New Year's Day premier league programme, Alan Shearer was the first to make his mark.

The England forward scored the first top flight goal of 1997, hammering home a volley from a corner after just four minutes against Leeds. He added a second in the 77th minute and Les Ferdinand scored a late third to ensure a 3-0 victory for Newcastle, a result which takes them into fourth.
Nottingham Forest moved off the bottom of the table with a 1-0 win at West Ham, pushing Southampton into last spot for the first time this season.
Fellow strugglers Blackburn also won away from home -- 2-0 at Everton -- to leave Middlesbrough, with a squad packed with big-name foreign signings, in the relegation zone.
